description: Engineering and product domains the skill catalog must cover. This list is meant to grow: add a domain here and the coverage test fails until a skill covers it. Each domain belongs to a company function; each function works in named phases (SKL-9). Both lists can grow.

functions.description: Product management: ideas, research, requirements, planning, analytics
Security: hardening, review, red / blue team
Compliance and audit: privacy, licences, audits
Data and ML: pipelines, analytics, models
Marketing and sales: positioning, outreach, pitching

domains.description: Designing whole systems: components, data flow, scaling, reliability, trade-offs
Module boundaries, decisions, design within a codebase
Server-side services, request handling, background jobs
Data modelling, schema design, queries, migrations

domains.note: Azure: Microsoft's official azure-deploy skill only works together with azure-prepare and azure-validate (about 200 files), so it is not bundled yet.

domains.description: Measuring and improving speed and resource use
Memory, CPU, concurrency, OS and hardware awareness
Building and operating LLM agents and tools
Desktop app packaging, code signing, installers and updates
Publishing to app stores and package registries, store review
domains.note: Apple App Store covered (asc skills, which need the unofficial asc CLI and the person's App Store Connect API key). Google Play: no vetted skill yet; Google's play-policy-insights depends on its Python scripts, including a store scraper.

domains.description: On-call, incident handling, postmortems, capacity planning (SRE)
domains.note: Incident handling, status updates and blameless postmortems covered. System capacity planning: no vetted skill yet (Anthropic's capacity-plan is about team capacity, not systems).
compliance-check covers GDPR, CCPA/CPRA and other privacy laws but not India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023. Licence compliance: no dedicated skill yet.

domains.description: Accessibility audits and testing (WCAG conformance checks)
End-to-end test strategy, load and stress testing
domains.note: Load, stress and functional checks covered by k6. Microsoft's playwright-cli is not bundled: its end-to-end test generation and test running live in reference files that would not ship, and it overlaps browser-testing-with-devtools.

domains.description: Measuring product use: events, funnels, experiments
Cost estimates, cloud cost, build-versus-buy (SWEBOK: software engineering economics)
domains.note: Vendor total cost of ownership (vendor-review) and AWS cost (aws-billing-and-cost-management) covered. Build-versus-buy for in-house work and other clouds: no vetted skill yet.

domains.description: Choosing a tech stack from the project's constraints, recorded as an ADR (STK)
Red-team / blue-team passes on the project itself (SEC)
Class and sequence design, design patterns, module internals (LLD)
Choosing and implementing algorithms and data structures (SWEBOK: computing foundations)
Protocols, sockets, HTTP, latency and offline behaviour
Internationalisation and localisation: languages, formats, right-to-left text
Maintaining and evolving existing and legacy code (SWEBOK: software maintenance)
Versions, baselines, environments and configuration (SWEBOK: configuration management)
Taking payments safely: providers, webhooks, refunds, compliance basics

pendingGapsNote: Domains not yet covered by a vetted skill (tasks A8-A10). The coverage test requires uncovered domains to match this list exactly, so it must shrink as gaps are filled and can never silently grow.

sources.name: SWEBOK v4 (IEEE Computer Society, 2024): 18 knowledge areas
ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 software life cycle processes (summary; the ISO site refuses automated reads)
OWASP SAMM model: 5 business functions, 15 practices
NIST Secure Software Development Framework (PO, PS, PW, RV)
Google SRE book, introduction (what SRE teams own)
NIST glossary: red team / blue team

sourcesNote: Checked against these on 2026-11-02 (owner's reviews of question 4 and of the second question set). The gap list came from that comparison.
